idiom_name: inherent method composed of private associated-function calls
implementation_notes: Rust methods live in impl blocks and items are private by default (visible only inside the defining module), so an fn whose body calls other methods of self is the ordinary realization; write pub(crate) or pub only when a step is genuinely shared. The borrow checker shapes the coordinator: &self and &mut self steps cannot overlap, so the sequence must finish each step before the next begins, and steps that would need conflicting borrows are better written as free functions in the module.
pitfalls: pub on a step is a permanent API commitment in a public crate (semver-visible); the default private visibility is what keeps the steps an implementation detail.
A step that returns a reference derived from self keeps the borrow alive, so later steps in the coordinator cannot take &mut self; return owned values or re-borrow explicitly.
If a step is a trait method, calling it from the coordinator adds a Self: Trait bound to the impl - inherent methods keep the coordinator free of extra bounds.
